subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack permanently use a fixed 30-second completion deadline for every bounded JSON REST operation while leaving FormData uploads without a fixed deadline?
rationale: The implementation is sound, but the exact deadline changes successful behavior for slow deployments and the multipart exception leaves a separate indefinite-wait path; repository evidence does not establish the ClickClack service contract needed to settle those policy choices automatically.

options.title: Approve the proposed policy
options.body: Accept the proven 30-second JSON deadline and size-based multipart exception, with the ambiguous write-timeout behavior treated as an owned ClickClack transport contract.

options.title: Retune before merge
options.body: Choose endpoint-specific or longer budgets and add focused proof for slow successful reads, write timeouts, and multipart behavior before landing.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it if ClickClack cannot guarantee useful completion and idempotency semantics under a fixed client deadline.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed policy
recommendation.body: Accept the proven 30-second JSON deadline and size-based multipart exception, with the ambiguous write-timeout behavior treated as an owned ClickClack transport contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a permanent compatibility and delivery-policy choice, and the available repository history most clearly identifies this account as the main merge and release decision owner.
